official_actual_P_commit.message:
Integrate installer ownership, archive pointer and sparse scan fixes

Compose the disjoint product and validation changes from reviewed PR195 and PR196. Retain PR196's existing source-review artifact as historical evidence. Preserve the PR195 source-binding seed pending an independent review and a separate final binding update for this actual combined tree. No original scale study, default budget or TODO status is changed.

original_creation_proof_locator.scope: root actual creation and official exact11-leaf readback; separate from independent current metadata reads

report.scope: Read-only review of sparse action representation, dense-reference tests, and the four production action consumers. No new execution, no whole-tree validation and no performance acceptance.
report.verdict: no new blocking correctness defect identified in this scope; current-head CI and combined source review remain required

findings.assessment: build_write_actions retains each parsed Add/Update exactly as the old dense map. The original scanned_paths set is passed separately to production dirty reconciliation. Full builds still perform no dirty promotion.

An explicit action takes precedence. A path absent from sparse actions is eligible for old Skip behavior iff the captured scanned_paths inventory contains it. Scoped scans retain surviving off-event DB paths and exclude admitted removals. This preserves the previous dense admission boundary, including scanned but unreadable or unparsed paths.

The unfinished-root test covers the union of explicit actions and scanned_paths, matching prior dense membership. Each promoted implicit Skip is materialized as DirtyResolveOnly before reload and write.

The consumers select Add/Update, Add, DirtyResolveOnly and DirtyResolveOnly respectively. They do not require explicit Skip entries. The changed-files, inventory, reload and write sets therefore retain their membership under the reviewed representation.

The wrapper passing an empty scanned set is cfg(test) and consumes dense actions. Production compute passes real scanned_paths. Retaining the old dense construction under cfg(test) provides a distinct reference implementation.

The added real-DB frontier test compares initial, resume and rebase histories at four budgets, including off-event imports, scanned-unparsed inputs, removed and unadmitted paths, explicit Add and full durable frontier equality. The separate ignored diagnostic times action-map construction and consumers only. This review read these tests; it did not execute them.

limits: No raw wall-clock, memory or whole-build gain is inferred from map sparsity.
The scan inventory, filesystem/hash/resolver work, admission and dirty budgets remain required.
Current PR196 CI was still in progress when this review began. Previous author local executions are not relabeled as execution on this head.
PR195 and PR196 share registry/guard binding paths. A future integration must regenerate full reviewed maps and source pins for the actual combined tree.

report.head: 065f5ab5da1bc5de74cbd3e4c360b51e09200687
report.scope: Only the five installer/helper/installer-CLI/archive-publisher/archive-test changed files. Root separately reviews scan; pr_triage reviews admission and CI. No whole-PR merge approval or execution credit.

findings.conclusion: The predicate is now exact PreToolUse + Grep|Glob|Search + type command + exact generated gate path. Substring mentions and differing event/matcher/type/command no longer suppress installation or qualify for hook removal.
findings.removal: Only matching command objects are removed; sibling hook objects, their unknown fields, unrelated events/matchers, and nonempty group annotations remain. Empty group is removed only if an owned command was removed.
findings.no_op: No settings rewrite occurs when no exact owned command is found. Exact already-installed hook avoids another settings rewrite/append.

findings.conclusion: Generic removal rejects nonobject root/section before writing; absent section/key preserves original bytes. Claude validates the settings root/hooks/selected event/entry shape before editing MCP or gate files on both install and uninstall.
findings.shape_scope: Validation permits arbitrary hook object fields and optional matcher, but requires present matcher to be string, event array, entry objects, and hooks arrays of objects. It validates the targeted event only. It does not claim to implement all external Claude configuration schemas.
findings.failure_scope: This is early validation for those malformed shapes, not a multi-file transaction. I/O errors or concurrent edits after preflight are not made atomic by this change.

findings.conclusion: For an initially absent latest, the new os.link uses a fully written, flushed/fsynced same-directory temporary file. Destination existence atomically causes failure instead of overwrite. The completed archive already exists and has been verified as an independent directory and remains available on pointer failure; CLI catches OSError and returns its error status. Temporary is removed in finally.
interleaving_reasoning: A observes no latest; B creates any latest after A writes temporary. A os.link raises FileExistsError and does not replace B bytes.
Both first publishers observe absence and finish their temp files. Exactly one link can create the same destination; loser preserves both already-created archive directories.
An existing eligible owned pointer follows the unchanged os.replace branch, preserving sequential advance behavior.
findings.new_filesystem_requirement: First publication needs same-filesystem hardlink support. An unsupported/filesystem error fails closed; there is no unsafe replace fallback. No cross-platform runtime was executed in this review.

coverage_review.assessment: The new vectors cover array/null roots and sections and absent/whitespace configurations with byte-equality assertions; existing malformed JSON tests remain.
Directly exercises substring false-positive, idempotence, matcher/event/type distinctions, user siblings and annotations, malformed targeted configuration before MCP/gate writes, and no-op bytes.
Real CLI tests statically cover install/uninstall status propagation and multiple persistent files. This review did not run them or independently confirm the PR body historical counts.

The first test injects a user file at the former race window and checks exact bytes/error2/retained verified archive/temp cleanup. The second barrier ensures both first publishers pass the initial absent observation, then requires one winner and both archives. Third checks existing-owned sequential advance. Prior symlink/unrelated and partial archive tests remain.

residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.origin: Inherited existing-owned replacement behavior; PR body explicitly limits the race fix to first publication.
residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.minimal_static_interleaving: A reads an owned latest and sets replace_owned=true. B replaces it with a regular unrelated user file. The second path check accepts a regular non-symlink, then A os.replace overwrites B.
residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.test_gap: New tests cover first-create races and sequential owned advance, not this interleaving. Do not claim all concurrent latest updates preserve user files.

residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.origin: Unchanged fixed-name installer behavior, not introduced by this PR.
residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.minimal_static_case: With valid empty settings and preexisting user bytes at .claude/hooks/codecortex-discovery-gate, install still writes that path and uninstall still removes it. The .mcp.json codecortex key is also treated as owned by key name. No payload marker/content ownership check is added.
residual_boundaries_not_new_patch_blocke.test_gap: New user-hook tests establish JSON entry preservation; they do not establish preservation of arbitrary user-created gate-file contents or colliding MCP entries.

No new interleaving or late I/O-failure rollback guarantee. Selected malformed-root/hooks/event cases are covered; inner malformed entry/matcher/hook-array variants are guarded in code but not all explicitly represented by new test vectors.

execution_and_acceptance_limits.conclusion: The five-file source changes are acceptable for their stated narrow ownership and first-create no-clobber scope. Existing CI and product acceptance requirements remain; no merge or TODO completion is inferred.

audit_receipt.scope: metadata/byte source review only; no product or original validator execution

method_boundary: Official current-P root plus non-truncated recursive metadata for exactly crates/scripts/tests/.github, with every supplied tree object reconstructed. Changed blob bytes directly recomputed. Unchanged SHA256 values inherited only when actual mode/type/Git blob/size exactly match the previously independently accepted GCW3 inventory. BASE before digests and membership follow the accepted complete GCW3 delta plus donor delta, with matching overlapping before values; no historical execution or all-history re-review is claimed.
retention: Existing donor reviews, large source archives, historical negative CI/CLI and raw study ZIPs remain at their original immutable Git locators. This support does not duplicate or overwrite them. Local API response copies may have a transport-added trailing newline; JSON contents are the original official response. Source blob bytes were separately checked by Git OID and SHA256.
